principle: Nothing below is claimed to be closed unless a named harness demonstrates it. Residual risk is stated as residual risk, not folded into the ceiling.
closed_by_this_return: MR-1 atomic admission under real multi-process concurrency
MR-2 un-droppable state transitions via sequence ownership
MR-3 blanket --auto eliminated; scoped permission profile enforced and proven load-bearing by control
MR-4 genuine kernel-enforced containment on this host, proven independent of application permissions
MR-5 commission delivery integrity: byte binding plus a dispatcher-generated authority frame
MR-6 lock reclaim by proven-dead owner; state directory fsync

residual_limitations_disclosed.limitation: Independent reviewer identity is NOT established.
residual_limitations_disclosed.detail: The governing review's own minimal-repair list requires a different model/variant or a different authority to occupy the reviewer role before unattended operation. That is a control outside the dispatcher's write terrain and outside this lane's authority; it cannot be self-certified here.
residual_limitations_disclosed.consequence: Unattended operation remains unqualified by this return regardless of the dispatcher repairs.

residual_limitations_disclosed.limitation: Seatbelt does not scope network egress by destination on this platform.
residual_limitations_disclosed.detail: The profile grants (allow network-outbound) because the seatbelt interface available here does not accept a host-scoped remote filter in the form attempted. Filesystem WRITE containment is the enforced boundary; egress is not destination-restricted.
residual_limitations_disclosed.consequence: A contained agent can still reach the network. Any claim of network containment would be false and is not made.

residual_limitations_disclosed.limitation: The child's own OpenCode session/cache directories remain writable inside the profile.
residual_limitations_disclosed.detail: OpenCode cannot function unless it may write its session, cache and config directories, so those paths are allow-listed. A determined adversary inside the sandbox could write there.
residual_limitations_disclosed.consequence: Containment is scoped to protecting the repository and the rest of the host, not to hermeticity against a hostile child.

residual_limitations_disclosed.detail: It is present and functional on this host (macOS 13.7.8) and the profile compiles and enforces, but Apple has deprecated Seatbelt and it may be absent on future releases.
residual_limitations_disclosed.consequence: The launcher probes for it and REFUSES to run rather than silently degrading to advisory-only. On a host without it, unattended operation is correctly blocked instead of being quietly downgraded.

residual_limitations_disclosed.limitation: The launcher's --agent argument does not resolve to a configured agent.
residual_limitations_disclosed.detail: A live run emitted 'agent "worker" not found. Falling back to default agent'. The dispatcher passes the role as --agent, but no agent by that name is configured, so agent-level role separation is not actually in effect. The permission profile is config-level and DOES apply, which is why out-of-terrain denial was enforced.
residual_limitations_disclosed.consequence: Role separation must not be credited to --agent. It currently rests on the scoped permission profile and the terrain gate. Configuring real per-role agents was outside this commission's scope and is not claimed.

residual_limitations_disclosed.limitation: Live end-to-end proof depends on provider reachability.
residual_limitations_disclosed.detail: The governing review recorded that live OpenCode E2E was not independently reproducible in its sandbox. On this host a real OpenCode process does run, so MR-3 and MR-5 acceptance were demonstrated against a genuine CLI process. That result is environment-dependent and is not a property of the code.
residual_limitations_disclosed.consequence: A reviewer without provider access can still re-run every pure-JS gate and the seatbelt enforcement checks, which need no provider.

residual_limitations_disclosed.limitation: Containment wraps the spawned child only.
residual_limitations_disclosed.detail: The dispatcher's own process is not sandboxed, and no OS user or ACL separation was introduced; the machine runs as a single user account.
residual_limitations_disclosed.consequence: The boundary is between the task agent and the rest of the host, not between accounts. Introducing a dedicated OS user was judged a disproportionate machine change and was deliberately not attempted.

residual_limitations_disclosed.limitation: The volume operated at 99% capacity with roughly 3.9-5.9 GiB free during this lane.
residual_limitations_disclosed.detail: Heavyweight execution was budgeted against this: no additional worktrees were created beyond the commissioned isolated one, duplicate fixture environments were avoided, and only lane-created disposable fixtures were reclaimed. Shared LOCAL_COURTS content and other lanes' worktrees were left untouched.
residual_limitations_disclosed.consequence: No phase was abandoned to ENOSPC, but the margin is thin and a reviewer should expect to budget for it.

explicitly_not_claimed: That the dispatcher is qualified for unattended source-free orchestration. It is not, and this return does not self-qualify it.
That worktree separation constitutes containment. It does not; kernel-enforced seatbelt containment is what was implemented and tested.
That network egress is contained. It is not.
That the agent is hermetically sealed. It is not.
That any gate passes by inspection. Every claim above names the harness that demonstrates it.
verification_method_notes: Concurrency claims are demonstrated with real OS processes, not simulated interleavings, because the original defect was timing-dependent.

The permission denial is demonstrated with a control experiment: the identical insisting prompt under external_directory:allow DID write the out-of-terrain file, so the denial under deny is attributable to the permission layer rather than to model reluctance.
Containment is demonstrated against a deliberately permissive OpenCode configuration so the kernel boundary is shown to be independent of application policy.

One early seatbelt result was a FALSE PASS caused by a profile that failed to compile; it was detected and corrected. It is recorded here because a containment claim that was never actually enforced is exactly the failure mode this lane exists to prevent.
